plants.name: Euphorbia pulcherrima
plants.description: A shrubby plant native to Mexico whose showy 'flowers' are actually colored bracts surrounding small yellow cyathia. In its native range it grows as a tall shrub, and in short winter days it develops its famous festive coloration.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to winter (November to February)
plants.location: Native to southern Mexico and Central America; cultivated worldwide as a holiday plant and in frost-free gardens
plants.funFact: The Aztecs called it 'cuetlaxochitl' and used its sap to make a reddish dye and as a fever remedy. Its color change is triggered by at least 12 hours of darkness per night.

plants.name: Helleborus niger
plants.description: An evergreen perennial from the buttercup family with nodding, cup-shaped white flowers that often age to pink. It blooms in the cold of early winter, sometimes pushing through snow.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early winter to early spring (December to March)
plants.location: Native to the mountains of central and southern Europe; grown in temperate gardens of Europe and North America
plants.funFact: Despite its name it is not a true rose. All parts are toxic, and in folklore the plant was said to have sprung from the tears of a girl who had no gift for the Christ child.

plants.name: Schlumbergera truncata
plants.description: An epiphytic cactus with flattened, segmented stems and arching, asymmetrical flowers. In Brazil it grows on tree branches and in rock crevices in cool, humid mountain forests.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to winter in the Northern Hemisphere (November to January); flowers in the Southern Hemisphere's late spring
plants.location: Native to the coastal mountains of southeastern Brazil near Rio de Janeiro; popular houseplant worldwide
plants.funFact: It is a short-day plant, so it sets buds when nights lengthen and temperatures cool. Its pollinators in the wild are hummingbirds.

plants.name: Delonix regia
plants.description: A broad, umbrella-shaped tree with feathery fern-like leaves that becomes covered in clusters of brilliant flowers. In the Southern Hemisphere's early summer it produces some of the most spectacular displays of any tropical tree.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to summer (October to January in the Southern Hemisphere; May to July in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to Madagascar; widely planted in tropical and subtropical regions including Australia, South Africa, Brazil and the Caribbean
plants.funFact: In its native Madagascar the species is endangered in the wild, even though it is one of the most widely planted ornamental trees in the world.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: A dense evergreen shrub with glossy dark leaves and delicate, lightly fragrant flowers. It starts blooming earlier than the common camellia and brightens gardens in late autumn and early winter.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn to early winter (October to January)
plants.location: Native to southern Japan; cultivated in the southeastern United States, Mediterranean, Australia and New Zealand
plants.funFact: Camellia sasanqua is related to the tea plant, and its seeds are pressed to produce camellia oil used in cooking and hair care in Japan.
